21:- Mouse hook (`WH_MOUSE_LL`): Applies Ctrl+Scroll zoom (persisted into the console font size setting for Command Prompt since v78.0, live-only for Windows Terminal — see the conhost zoom paragraph below); converts plain left-drag to SHIFT+drag for WT text selection. WT selection assist must run inline on the hook thread, not marshaled (issue #99, v53.0): `BeginWindowsTerminalSelectionTracking`/`UpdateWindowsTerminalSelectionTracking`/`ResetWindowsTerminalSelectionTracking` used to run on the UI thread via the same `Dispatcher.BeginInvoke` fire-and-forget marshal as the rest of `HandleMouseHookEvent`. Windows Terminal (and the app's own VT mouse tracking underneath it) decides per mouse message whether SHIFT is down at the moment it arrives to choose between local text selection and forwarding the drag to the app — so any queuing delay before the injected `keybd_event(VK_SHIFT)` lands (arbitrarily long whenever the VS UI thread is busy, the exact scenario `_hookThread` from issue #61 exists to route around) meant the app frequently already owned the drag by the time SHIFT arrived, silently breaking selection/copy. Fixed by calling these three directly from `LowLevelMouseHookCallback` for `WM_LBUTTONDOWN`/`WM_MOUSEMOVE`/`WM_LBUTTONUP`, synchronously on the hook thread; the hit test moved to `IsScreenPointInsideTerminalWindow` (plain `GetWindowRect(terminalHandle, …)`, no WPF/WinForms — mirrors `TryForwardConhostCtrlZoom`'s pattern) since the WinForms-touching `IsScreenPointInsideActiveTerminalPanel` isn't safe off the UI thread. `WM_MOUSEMOVE`/`WM_LBUTTONUP` are no longer marshaled to the UI thread at all (`ShouldDispatchMouseHookMessage` only forwards `WM_LBUTTONDOWN`, still needed there for `ActivateEmbeddedTerminalOnClick`); the selection-tracking bookkeeping fields (`_windowsTerminalSelectionPending`/`_windowsTerminalSelectionActive`/`_windowsTerminalSelectionModifierInjected`/`_windowsTerminalSelectionStartPoint`) are now touched exclusively from the single hook thread. WT copy matches Command Prompt: drag to select, right-click to copy (issue #99 follow-up, same v53.0): fixing the timing race made SHIFT-drag reliably highlight text, but a reporter came back twice more — first that there was no way to copy a highlight at all, then (after an interim fix auto-copied on mouse-up via an injected Ctrl+Shift+C) that copying *and clearing* the selection the instant the mouse button was released was "strange" and didn't match Command Prompt's model of drag-to-select-and-keep-it-highlighted, right-click-to-copy-and-clear. `ResetWindowsTerminalSelectionTracking` (`WM_LBUTTONUP`) now only releases the injected SHIFT, if any — it no longer sends any copy keystroke, so a selection survives past mouse-up exactly like conhost. Copy-on-right-click is delegated entirely to Windows Terminal's own global `rightClickAction` setting rather than reintroduced as a hook-based right-click interceptor (which is exactly the design issue #90 already ruled out, see below): `EnsureWindowsTerminalRightClickCopyPaste()` patches WT's `settings.json` to set `"rightClickAction": "copyPaste"` once (mirrors `EnsureWindowsTerminalFontProfile`'s parse/mutate-if-different/write pattern, called unconditionally on every WT launch, cheap no-op once already set) — WT then natively copies-and-clears an active selection on right-click, or pastes when there's no selection, with no extension-side keystroke injection or right-click hooking at all. Conhost Ctrl+Scroll zoom is input-mode-independent (issue #76/#78): for the Command Prompt terminal (`_wtTabBarHeight == 0`), `TryForwardConhostCtrlZoom` runs on the hook thread (Win32 `GetWindowRect` hit test, no WPF/WinForms), consumes the physical wheel (returns 1), and changes the console font size directly via `SetCurrentConsoleFontEx` (`TryAdjustConhostFontSize`), then schedules the repaint on the UI thread. The size the zoom settles on is persisted (v78.0): once the drain worker has emptied the notch accumulator it converts the resulting cell height back to points (`ConsoleCellHeightPxToFontPt`, the exact inverse of the `ConsoleFontPtToCellHeightPx` used when writing the launch-time registry value, clamped to the 6–36 pt the Settings combo offers) and writes it to `ConsoleFontSizePt` via `PersistConhostZoomFontSize` + `SaveSettings`, so the next session opens at that size with no trip to Settings. Persisting after the drain (not per notch) keeps a fast scroll from rewriting the settings file dozens of times. Deliberately conhost-only: Windows Terminal handles Ctrl+Scroll internally and the gesture never reaches the extension, so there is no size to capture there. This is not a revival of the v73.0 auto-zoom replay — nothing replays a *delta* at startup; the terminal simply launches at a normal configured font size. `PersistConhostZoomFontSize` omits the usual `ThrowIfNotOnUIThread` guard on purpose: it would mark the method UI-thread-only for the analyzer, which then propagates the requirement up through the drain worker to the mouse-hook callback that legitimately runs off-thread. Notches are coalesced (v73.0, fixes occasional freeze/runaway on fast scroll): instead of spawning a `Task.Run` font-change per wheel notch, each notch does `Interlocked.Add(ref _pendingConhostZoomSteps, ±1)` and ensures a single drain worker (`_conhostZoomWorkerActive` 0/1 flag, `StartConhostZoomDrainWorker`) is running. The worker `Exchange`s the accumulated total, applies it in one `TryAdjustConhostFontSize(steps)` call, waits ~25 ms for more notches to accumulate, then re-checks and loops; it releases the flag and re-acquires via `CompareExchange` so a notch landing in the gap is never stranded. This matters because each `TryAdjustConhostFontSize` does an `AttachConsole`/`FreeConsole` under `_consoleSnapshotLock` and every attach briefly bounces the conhost's keyboard focus — one attach per fast-scroll burst instead of N stops the focus churn that made the zoom freeze/run away. `TryAdjustConhostFontSize` returns the signed notches actually applied (fewer than requested at the min/max clamp bound, 0 on no-change/failure) so the drain worker's loop bookkeeping stays exact at the clamp bound. The earlier v19 approach of posting `WM_MOUSEWHEEL + MK_CONTROL` to the conhost window did not work once a TUI put the console into mouse-input mode (QuickEdit off): conhost forwards both the physical wheel and a posted wheel to the app as input records, so neither reaches conhost's own zoom — that's why zoom worked only before the agent's TUI came up. Setting the font is independent of console input mode, so it works whether the TUI is up or not. WT is left on its native path (dispatch → `HandleMouseHookEvent`, which now only repaints the embedded panel after WT's native wheel zoom). Right-click is no longer intercepted at all (v29.0, root-fix for issue #90): the hook does not touch `WM_RBUTTONDOWN`/`WM_RBUTTONUP` — conhost/Windows handle the right mouse button natively everywhere (context menus in the editor/Solution Explorer, conhost's own QuickEdit-on right-click paste). The earlier "conhost right-click paste fallback" (issues #78/#82/#83) consumed right-clicks via a global `WH_MOUSE_LL` hook to paste into the agent's TUI when QuickEdit was off; despite an occlusion-aware + foreground-gated hit test it kept mis-firing — a right-click elsewhere in VS would be swallowed and the clipboard pushed into the console (issue #90) — so the whole feature was removed (`TryConhostRightClickPaste`, `IsScreenPointOverTerminalWindow`, `_consumeNextRButtonUp`, `_conhostInMouseInputMode` cache + `QueueConhostMouseInputModeRefresh`, and the `WM_RBUTTONDOWN/UP` constants are all gone). Pasting into the agent goes through the prompt box, whose send path delivers via `PasteViaConhostPasteCommandAsync` (conhost's own Edit→Paste `WM_COMMAND/ID_CONSOLE_PASTE` posted straight to `terminalHandle`) regardless of QuickEdit/mouse-input mode — so no terminal right-click paste is needed. `PasteViaConhostPasteCommandAsync` and `IsTerminalInMouseInputMode()` remain, now used only by the send path (the mouse-input-mode probe still drives whether the send path injects its pre-deselect right-click). TUI Fullscreen removed, Claude Code always launches classic (v53.0): the model-menu "TUI Fullscreen" toggle (`TuiFullscreenEnableMenuItem`/`TuiFullscreenDisableMenuItem`, `SendTuiModeCommandAsync`, `ClaudeCodeSettings.ClaudeTuiFullscreen`) is gone — `GetClaudeCommand()` now unconditionally prefixes the launch with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1` instead of branching on a persisted tri-state setting. This also retired the issue #96 fullscreen-only mouse-wheel-to-PgUp/PgDn forwarding (`IsClaudeFullscreenConhostActive`, `GetFullscreenWheelScrollKeystrokeCount`, `SendScrollKeyToTerminal`, `TryEnsureFullscreenLineScrollKeybinding`/`AddBindingIfAbsent` and the `keybindings.json` line-scroll installer) since fullscreen (alternate-screen) rendering can no longer be entered through the extension, making that whole path permanently unreachable; `ShouldDispatchMouseHookMessage`'s `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` case now dispatches only for Ctrl held, and `HandleMouseHookEvent`'s wheel branch lost its plain-wheel-forward `else if`. Ctrl+Scroll zoom hijacked other apps when VS wasn't foreground (v51.0): both zoom paths — `TryForwardConhostCtrlZoom` (conhost) and the `ctrlDown` branch of `HandleMouseHookEvent` (Windows Terminal) — only hit-tested the cursor against the terminal's screen rectangle, which stays valid even when another maximized window is now layered on top of that same screen region (VS backgrounded). Global `WH_MOUSE_LL` doesn't know z-order, so Ctrl+Scroll in that other app got silently redirected into zooming the (invisible) embedded terminal instead of reaching the app the user was actually looking at. Fixed by extracting `IsTerminalHostForeground()` (the `GetForegroundWindow() == terminalHandle || hostRoot` check, previously inlined at the top of `IsTerminalFocused()`) and requiring it in both zoom paths before the rect hit test runs — cheap enough for the hook thread (same GetForegroundWindow-based short-circuit `IsTerminalFocused()` already relied on). Deliberately stops short of requiring full `IsTerminalFocused()` (keyboard focus on the terminal control specifically) so hover-to-zoom while VS is foreground still works without first clicking into the terminal.
22:- Classic-mode mouse tracking disabled unconditionally (v112.0, issues #118/#119): `GetClaudeCommand()`'s always-classic launch prefix (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1`, v53.0 above) now always adds `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1` too, for both the cmd.exe and WSL command-prefix forms. Current Claude Code CLI builds turn on terminal mouse tracking (conhost QuickEdit disabled / `ENABLE_MOUSE_INPUT`) even in the classic renderer — confirmed by `IsTerminalInMouseInputMode()` (the paste path's probe) detecting QuickEdit-off sessions with no fullscreen involved. With mouse tracking on, conhost forwards the physical wheel to Claude's stdin as mouse-report escape sequences instead of scrolling its own buffer, so the wheel did nothing while the agent was generating (#118, "can't scroll up to see earlier output") and, on long/busy sessions, likely fed the fast-input heuristic stray escape data that rendered as garbled/overlapping text (#119). Same fix already proven for fullscreen under issue #92 (above) — now unconditional since fullscreen no longer exists to gate it on.
23:- Windows Terminal runaway-zoom guard (v94.0, issue #117): unlike the conhost path — where `TryAdjustConhostFontSize` hard-clamps the cell height — WT owns its Ctrl+Scroll zoom entirely and has no ceiling, so nothing bounded it. Reporters described the font "progressively growing till it is huge" shortly after load and self-resolving later, the fingerprint of a notch burst (real or spuriously synthesized) arriving far faster than a human could scroll. There is no simple API to read or reset WT's own zoom level, so `IsRunawayWtZoomBurst` instead counts Ctrl+wheel notches over the terminal in a rolling window (`WtZoomBurstWindowMs` 1500 / `WtZoomBurstMaxNotches` 30) and, once the burst clears that generous ceiling, `LowLevelMouseHookCallback` returns 1 to swallow the notch before WT ever sees it — bounding the damage regardless of what triggered the burst. Gated on `_wtTabBarHeight > 0` (WT only), `IsTerminalHostForeground()` and the `GetWindowRect` hit test, the same trio the zoom paths already use; the counters are `Volatile`/`Interlocked` because this runs on the hook thread
33:- TUI fullscreen env vars (v31/v32, `GetClaudeCommand`): `_settings.ClaudeTuiFullscreen` (nullable) injects an env prefix ahead of the `claude` command — `true` → `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` plus `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1`; `false` → `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1` (classic renderer); `null` → nothing (CLI default). cmd.exe form is `set X=1 && set Y=1 && {cmd}`, WSL bash form is `X=1 Y=1 {cmd}`. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE` is mandatory whenever fullscreen is on (issue #92): fullscreen rendering enables Claude Code's own terminal mouse tracking, which in the embedded conhost — where the extension already runs a global mouse hook and re-asserts focus — emits a continuous burst of mouse-input escape sequences that Claude's fast-input heuristic collapses into `[Pasted text +N lines]` bracketed-paste blocks, flooding the prompt on launch and on every restart. The extension supplies its own mouse zoom / click-to-focus / paste, so disabling Claude's mouse capture loses nothing while keeping the flicker-free draw. The one casualty is wheel scrolling: with Claude's mouse off, the wheel no longer pages the conversation (per Claude's docs, fullscreen + `DISABLE_MOUSE` keeps only the keyboard scroll keys `PgUp`/`PgDn`/`Ctrl+Home`/`Ctrl+End`, plus native terminal selection of the visible viewport). Wheel scroll restored without re-enabling Claude's mouse (v36, issue #96): the global mouse hook's `HandleMouseHookEvent` now, on a plain (no-Ctrl) wheel notch over the active panel when `IsClaudeFullscreenConhostActive()`, posts `VK_PRIOR`/`VK_NEXT` (PgUp/PgDn) keystrokes to the terminal via `SendScrollKeyToTerminal`. Two gotchas: (1) `ShouldDispatchMouseHookMessage` must let the plain wheel through — it otherwise forwards `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` only when Ctrl is held (zoom), so the plain-wheel case is gated on `IsClaudeFullscreenConhostActive()` there too, or the handler never runs. (2) `SendScrollKeyToTerminal` builds a real `lParam` (scan code from `MapVirtualKey` + extended-key bit) — conhost silently drops a posted key with a zero scan code instead of translating it to VT input (`ESC[5~`/`ESC[6~`). Posted straight to `terminalHandle` (focus-independent, like the Enter path); gated to conhost (`_wtTabBarHeight <= 0`) and the Claude Code / Claude Code (WSL) providers so it never hijacks conhost's own scrollback in the classic renderer or Windows Terminal's native wheel handling. Smooth line scroll (vs. the half-page PgUp default): for *native* Claude Code, `TryEnsureFullscreenLineScrollKeybinding()` merges `pageup`→`scroll:lineUp`, `pagedown`→`scroll:lineDown` (and `shift+pageup/pagedown`→`scroll:halfPage*` to preserve paging) into `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\keybindings.json` — those line-scroll actions are unbound by default, so the wheel had nothing finer than half-page to trigger. With the binding in place each notch sends one PgUp/PgDn (`GetFullscreenWheelScrollKeystrokeCount()` returns 1) for a one-line step; WSL Claude (config lives in the WSL filesystem) and any write failure fall back to a single half-page keystroke. The keybinding file is touched once per session, lazily on first wheel scroll, and merges without overwriting existing user bindings (`AddBindingIfAbsent`).
59:**A second review of the branch then found nine more places where the repair worked against itself; all nine are fixed here and covered by `Tests/ConsoleGridFitTests.cs` and `Tests/ConsoleCellDpiScalingTests.cs`.** (a) *The painted cell has a second source, and an unmeasured one now stops the fit.* `EstimatePaintedConsoleCell` fell back to the reported size whenever `dwMaximumWindowSize` was capped by the buffer rather than the screen — which is the permanent state of the **alternate screen buffer**, where every full-screen agent UI runs and the buffer *is* the viewport — and the caller went on computing a grid from that known-wrong value. Fed the reported 6x13 px of a console painting 12x26, the fit asks for 135 columns where 67 fit, `BufferMustGrow` fires, conhost sizes its own window to the wider buffer, and the window re-apply right after narrows it straight back, dropping every column past the panel: the repair inflicting the exact damage it exists to prevent, reachable from a plain `SessionUnlock` with no display change at all. The estimate now takes `clientWidthPx / viewCols` as a second source — the painted column pitch, measured off the window the host laid that grid into, which survives the collapse because only *rows* collapse — and reports through `measured` / `ConsoleGridSnapshot.PaintedCellMeasured` whether either source answered. `TryFitConsoleGridToWindow` refuses to compute a grid from an unmeasured cell, and the snapshot overload of `TryComputeConsoleGridFit` carries the same guard. (b) *Rows are no longer clamped to the buffer.* `targetRows = Math.Min(targetRows, bufferRows)` is invisible in the main buffer (thousands of rows deep) and fatal in the alternate one: it pinned a viewport that had collapsed to 6 rows at 6 rows forever, the read-back then compared 6 against 6 and found nothing wrong, the line was marked routine and discarded, and the last pass never raised the notice. The buffer grows with the viewport instead — `BufferMustGrow` covers both dimensions and `SetConsoleScreenBufferSize` takes `Math.Max` against what is there, so like columns the rows only ever grow. (c) *A clamped rescale is not a success.* `ScaleConsoleCellHeightForDpi` returns 0 both when nothing was owed and when the zoom clamp refused the ratio, and the DPI mode reported the unchanged height either way — so the repair adopted the new DPI, `_terminalCellDpi` began lying about the cell, the width guard fell, and the next resize narrowed conhost against cells that were still the old size. The partial clamp was worse and had no path at all: a 8 px cell halving to a clamped 6 is a real change reported as a full one. `IdealConsoleCellHeightForDpi` (pure, unit-tested) supplies the unclamped target, `ConsoleCellRescale.ReachedTargetHeight` tells the two apart, and only a rescale that reached its target adopts the DPI; one that did not keeps the guard on, logs `clamped at Npx … width will be held`, and on the last pass reaches the info bar through `gridCouldNotBeRepaired` — which is also why `FitConsoleGridAfterRepairAsync` now *returns* its verdict instead of raising the bar itself. (d) *The Ctrl+Scroll zoom no longer persists what the repair corrected.* The drain worker saves an absolute cell height, so the first wheel notch after a rescale wrote the DPI-corrected cell into `ConsoleFontSizePt` — a DPI-independent value applied at every later launch. One click after a 200%→100% reconnect halved the console font for good, on every display. `_conhostDpiCellOffsetPx` accumulates `ConsoleCellRescale.DeltaPx` and is subtracted before persisting, so what is saved is the size the user zoomed to measured against the size they had picked; it resets with the terminal. (e) *The WT tab-bar refresh reads the panel DPI.* `GetWtTabBarHeight()` went through `GetDpiForWindow(terminalHandle)` — the stale source `GetTerminalPanelDpi` exists to replace — so the re-evaluation this branch added was either a no-op (host still reporting the old DPI) or actively wrong (halving `_wtTabBarHeight` on a 200%→100% reconnect while WT paints a 96 px bar, leaving 48 px of tab bar visible). There is now a `GetWtTabBarHeight(uint panelDpi)` overload and the pass passes the DPI it already holds. (f) *The width hold is captured once, and a failed rescale is retried.* `minWidth = GetEmbeddedTerminalWidth()` re-read the live window rect on every resize, so once a fit left conhost sizing its own window wider than the panel, that width became the new floor and the splitter could never pull it back — a ratchet. `_heldTerminalWidthPx` captures it at the moment the DPIs first disagree and clears when they agree again. The second half: `_lastDisplayRepairDpi` was set at the *top* of pass 0, before anything had been attempted, so a rescale that failed for a passing reason (console unreachable while the agent restarts) locked the terminal at the old width for the rest of its life. `ShouldScheduleDisplayRepairFromResize` bounds the retries by `MaxDisplayRepairCyclesPerDpi` and `DisplayRepairRetryCooldownMs` (15 s, longer than a full 12.75 s cycle) instead, and `NoteDisplayRepairScheduled` closes the gate *in the resize handler* rather than 150 ms later in the pass — which also ends the relayout storm, where every resize arriving inside those 150 ms wrote a `LogTerminalLaunch` line on the UI thread and superseded the pass that was about to repair. (g) *A buffer that grew counts as changed.* Both "viewport refused" paths returned `Changed = false` although `SetConsoleScreenBufferSize` had already succeeded, so the caller skipped the window re-apply for a console conhost had already resized itself to — and no later pass recovered it, because by then the buffer is wide and nothing asks to grow it. `bufferChanged` carries into every outcome after the write. (h) *An unmeasurable grid is not a healthy one.* Both "could not read it" exits reported `Changed` and `StillOff` clear, which is the signature of *nothing to repair*: the quiet-cycle summary then swallowed the one line a bug report needs, and the last pass stayed silent over a terminal painting six rows of its panel. `ConsoleGridFitOutcome.Measured` distinguishes them and the routine predicate requires it. (i) *The size nudge is in painted pixels.* `ConsoleSizeNudgeHeightPx` was `ConhostZoomMaxPx`, a bound on the *reported* cell, applied as an overshoot in *painted* ones — the unit confusion this whole area is about. On a console painting at 200% with a zoomed cell the nudge stays inside the row the host already has, reports nothing, and leaves the agent drawing against a stale row count: the failure `forceSizeNotification` was added for. It is `ConhostZoomMaxPx * MaxPaintedCellScale` now, and the surplus is clipped by the panel for the single call it lives in.
136:- Round 3 of the same F5 pass (still v170.0): the composer's own 📎 `ComposerAttachButton`/`AttachRequested` was removed outright — Ctrl+V paste and drag-and-drop already attach a file or image, so the button added nothing that wasn't already reachable, and it made even less sense once the panel's own `AttachDropdownButton` (with its "Insert Active File Path" entry) was already gone from view whenever the chat is detached (see the `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` collapse above). Its removal took `OnComposerAttachRequested` (NativeChat.cs) and both of its event subscriptions with it; `OnComposerFilesDropped`/`OnComposerPasteRequested` are untouched. Separately, the action row's `DockPanel` is now wrapped in a `ScrollViewer` (`ComposerActionsScroller`, `HorizontalScrollBarVisibility="Auto"`) — a customized toolbar plus every selector and mirrored config button can be wider than the tab, and the row used to clip silently past the window edge with no way to reach what didn't fit. `ComposerActionsScroller_PreviewMouseWheel` remaps the mouse wheel (vertical by default, and there is nothing vertical in this row for it to act on) to `ScrollToHorizontalOffset`, only when `ScrollableWidth > 0` so the event still bubbles normally everywhere else.
137:- Round 4 of the same F5 pass (still v170.0), from a follow-up screenshot: two more complaints. First, "the button for attach/detach should never show for native mode" — a direct reversal of Change D above, which had forced ⧉ `DetachToolbarButton` always visible in native mode specifically so there was a way back to the chat tab. `RefreshToolbarLayout()` now gates it the opposite way: `Apply(ToolbarButton.DetachTerminal, !IsNativeModeActive, DetachToolbarButton, DetachTerminalMenuItem)` hides it unconditionally whenever native mode is active, whether the chat is docked or already in its own tab (the old `if (id == ToolbarButton.DetachTerminal) continue;` carve-out in the `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` collapse loop is gone too — redundant once ⧉ is already hidden earlier in the method). Each arrow starts `Collapsed` and is toggled by a new `ComposerActionsScroller_ScrollChanged` handler reading `ScrollableWidth`/`HorizontalOffset`, so an arrow only appears when there's actually more content to reach in that direction — no permanently-visible dead-end arrows, and no native scrollbar track competing for space in a row this thin. 703:- Markdown is rendered, not split (`UI/MarkdownFlowRenderer.cs`): headings, block quotes as a bordered `Section` whose `>`-stripped lines go through `BuildBlocks` again, so lists, code, tables and nested quotes work inside them and quoted lines keep their line breaks (v273.0; lazy continuation lines without `>` are not supported), lists (nested, ordered and unordered; task items `[ ]`/`[x]` show a read-only empty square (U+1F532 dark frame on a light theme, U+1F533 light frame on a dark one — `IsLightText` on the block's text brush, so the extension's forced theme counts too and a theme switch, which changes `Foreground`, rebuilds it) or a check emoji (U+2705 green on a light theme, the softer purple U+2611 U+FE0F on a dark one, same `IsLightText` test), after the list's own bullet or number — v273.0; both runs are pinned to Segoe UI Emoji, so they share the emoji glyph width whatever the chat font is (the earlier U+2610 text symbol came from another fallback font and was narrower) and the check renders green, where a symbol font like Segoe UI Symbol would draw a monochrome outline), block quotes, rules, pipe tables (column alignment from the separator row's colons, `ParseTableAlignments`, v273.0; an escaped `\|` stays in its cell), fenced code and the inline runs (`bold`, `*italic*`, `~~strikethrough~~` (v273.0, a `Span` with `TextDecorations.Strikethrough`), `***both***`, `` `code` ``, links; v273.0: a marker run closes only on a run long enough that does not follow whitespace, taking its last characters as the closer, an italic skips nested `**` runs and code spans are skipped — `FindEmphasisCloser` — so `***x***` no longer left a stray `*` that italicised the rest of the line; v273.0: CommonMark backslash escapes — `IsEscapable` ASCII punctuation becomes literal, also for the closer search, and a backslash before anything else is kept, so `C:\Users` reads as written) become a `FlowDocument` shown by `MarkdownBlock`, a read-only `FlowDocumentScrollViewer`. lines: - The transcript list owns its `ScrollViewer` through the `ItemsControl` template, with a `VirtualizingStackPanel` and pixel scrolling, so only rows in view are realized. `ShowNativeChatTabAsync` runs before a resumed transcript is replayed: an invisible list realizes every replayed row at once (measured 76 s for 72 messages / 156 rows), while a visible virtualized list realizes only what fits. Rows use `Standard` virtualization with a `2,2`-page `CacheLength`, so deferred Markdown is measured before it scrolls into view and a recycled container cannot flash the previous row's height.

- Each row container (`ItemContainerStyle`) is sized to the transcript `ScrollViewer`'s `ViewportWidth`, left-aligned (v276.0): after the tab shrank the virtualizing panel could keep rows at their old width, pushing a card's right-aligned Skip/Submit buttons out of view. While the viewport is still 0 (before the first layout) the row stays auto-sized.

- Markdown is parsed when a row is loaded (`MarkdownBlock.DeferRenderingUntilLoaded`), not when its data template is created; collapsed tool bodies defer separately (`DeferRenderingWhenCollapsed`). This keeps a long replay/scroll from parsing hundreds of documents up front.

-- Wheel scrolling is claimed by the transcript (`PreviewMouseWheel` on `MessagesList`) before a message's `FlowDocumentScrollViewer` can consume it; a deliberately scrollable nested pane (a diff) keeps the wheel while it can still move.

+- Wheel scrolling is claimed by the transcript (`PreviewMouseWheel` on `MessagesList`) before a message's `FlowDocumentScrollViewer` can consume it; a deliberately scrollable nested pane (a diff) keeps the wheel while it can still move Since v305.0 (issue #262) `FindVerticalScrollTarget` picks that pane by walking up past every scroller whose vertical bar is disabled or has nothing to scroll (each `MarkdownBlock`/code block has a disabled one sized to its content — stopping there sent the wheel over the plan review box's text to the transcript), and `Transcript_PreviewMouseWheel` scrolls the pane itself (`VerticalWheelTarget`, 16 px per wheel line, a page when Windows scrolls a screen at a time) because the markdown viewer's inner scroller would otherwise consume the wheel.

- A replayed conversation opens at its newest message: both replay paths call `ScrollToLatest`, which forces following and repeats `ScrollToEnd` on dispatcher passes until the measured bottom is reached. Live follow is capped at two passes (one follow-up for a still-estimated extent; the next streamed line requests another), while forced scrolls keep up to six.

- Shift+wheel scrolls sideways (v274.0): `Transcript_PreviewMouseWheel` first looks for the closest scroller under the pointer that can move sideways (`FindHorizontalScrollTarget`: horizontal bar not disabled, `ScrollableWidth` > 0, not the transcript) — a code block's nested `MarkdownBlock`, raw tool input/output (`IsNoWrap`), a tool card's diff pane. A `FlowDocumentScrollViewer` keeps its `ScrollViewer` inside its template, and walking up from the pointer's document content reaches the viewer past it, so that one is looked up downwards. The step is the vertical one (16 px per wheel line, wheel down = right, `HorizontalWheelTarget`). Nothing to scroll sideways under the pointer: the wheel scrolls the transcript as usual. A horizontal touchpad swipe (`WM_MOUSEHWHEEL`) is not handled — WPF on .NET Framework has no event for it.

- Following is the reader's choice, not an offset comparison: `_readerTookOver` is set only by a wheel turn that scrolls the transcript or a press on the transcript's own scrollbar (`TemplatedParent` check, so a nested scrollbar does not count). Layout growth — virtualized height estimates, a Markdown block realizing rows — never clears it. A settle timer restarts on each input and only resumes following when it expires with the view at the bottom; sending a prompt calls `ScrollToLatest`, which clears the flag so the new answer is visible.
